provenance.user_quote: Each courier is on the roster under exactly one name.
A courier without a name on the roster is not a courier.
A courier reports to one home depot.
Every route leaves from a single depot.
A courier is rostered onto a route once; no duplicate rosterings.

provenance.user_note: A route carries between one and three rostered couriers.

provenance.user_quote: One weigh-in per parcel.
A parcel shows one current status.
A delivery carries one parcel.
A delivery cannot exist without its parcel.
A delivery runs on one route.
One courier owns a delivery end to end.
One stop tally per delivery.
A delivery is identified by its parcel and its route together.
Status is one of pending, in-transit, delivered or returned.

constraints.rationale: A single courier lifts a parcel unaided, so parcel weight is capped at 30 kg.

provenance.matched_pattern: weight value type on a courier-carried parcel

constraints.rationale: No courier is simultaneously on shift and off duty.

object_types.name: ContractorEmployee
object_types.derivation_rule: Each ContractorEmployee is an Employee who is not full-time and not part-time.

provenance.user_quote: Each employee has exactly one registered name.
Every employee must have a name on file.
One recorded gender per employee.
Each employee has a single current salary.
Each employee reports to at most one manager.

constraints.rationale: Reporting chains do not loop back on themselves in a sane org chart.

provenance.user_note: Confirmed: nobody is their own manager.

provenance.user_quote: An employee is on a project once; no duplicate memberships.

provenance.user_note: Teams are capped at ten members.

constraints.rationale: A project normally has a single lead.

provenance.user_quote: A department has exactly one head.
An assignment belongs to one employee.
An assignment cannot exist without its employee.
An assignment targets one project.
One running hours total per assignment.
A project has one recorded run interval.

constraints.rationale: A project cannot end before it starts.

provenance.user_quote: An assignment is identified by its employee and project together.

constraints.rationale: Employees are expected to either work on a project or head a department.

provenance.rationale_world_fact: Organizations assign staff to productive roles; idle headcount is exceptional.

provenance.user_quote: Gender is recorded as M, F, or X.

constraints.rationale: Logged hours are non-negative and bounded by a sanity cap.
Overtime is a small fraction of total logged hours.

provenance.rationale_world_fact: Labor regulations cap overtime well below regular working hours.

provenance.user_note: An employee appears in at most four project engagements.

constraints.rationale: Whoever leads a project also works on that project.
An assignment always has both an employee and a project side.
No employee is simultaneously active and terminated.
Every employee is either full-time or part-time, never both.

provenance.user_note: The company runs between one and twelve departments.
At most twelve employees head departments (one per department).

constraints.rationale: Every employee is engaged either as a contractor or permanently.

constraints.expression: Each Employee who heads a Department must be a PermanentEmployee.

warnings.message: the 'textual' constraint 'Each Employee who heads a Department must be a PermanentEmployee.' carries modality 'alethic', but its family can never be mechanically evaluated — so this model can never reach exit 0 for ANY population: an unverifiable HARD constraint means acceptance cannot be mechanically claimed, and the run is permanently indeterminate (exit 4). Write 'modality: deontic' unless permanent indeterminacy is what you intend (D-20).

provenance.user_quote: An expense is in exactly one state at a time.
Every expense has a state from the moment it is filed.
One approver signs off on an expense.
One expense reaches Workday once.
A chain has one approval threshold.

provenance.anchor: ### Effect atomicity — why there is no `replace`

provenance.user_quote: Only a draft can be approved.
Nothing reaches Workday before approval.
We only pay what Workday has.
We like to know who signed it off.
Finance likes to see the approver on file.
Nothing reaches Workday before approval.
